correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the statement exactly by Lucas to minimal zero-sum digit tokens; an explicit prefix-sum/swapping proof establishes the cyclic length-m classification. The finite-profile formula counts all digit placements without duplication and removes the sole excluded N=m row. Polynomial degrees and the order-h coefficient are proved symbolically; all-X comparison follows by neighboring base-p powers. The supplied standalone verifier reproduced 11,866 direct Lucas equivalences, 763,424 length-m zero-sum word tests and exact-profile row counts in five families; no finite check is substituted for an infinite proof. The order-four branch formulas have degree-at-most-five polynomial-identity certificates at six points per branch.

value.rationale: Sharp extremal valuations motivate the independent quantitative question of how often any positive valuation occurs. The complete family-wide eventual quasipolynomial, with explicit finite profile and a leading coefficient controlled by multiplicative order, quantifies a natural exact invariant and establishes extreme polylogarithmic sparsity. It covers all coprime pairs including genuine h>=3 cases beyond the previously classified congruence classes, and is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a known-table recomputation. The explicit (m,p)=(5,2) instance has exact eventual quasipolynomial period four, detected by two distinct polynomial branches.
